name: STAK Energy Campus Gas Pipeline
monitor_reason: no concrete step and no endpoints: the state land lease application covers only the campus site, the pipeline is not part of it, and neither route, length nor gas source is set
researcher_notes: STAK Energy has applied to the Alaska Division of Oil and Gas for a 50-year lease on about 715 acres near Dalton Highway milepost 390, roughly 26 road miles south of Deadhorse, for a campus of up to 3 gigawatts. A DatacenterDynamics article from May 2026 and a Petroleum News story from June 2026 both say the campus would be fed by new gas pipelines that are still being planned, from fields about 25 to 90 miles away. The pipeline is not part of the lease application and would need its own approval. No route, length, diameter, owner of the pipe or gas supplier has been named. This is not an existing GEM row: the nearby North Slope rows are long-haul or Point Thomson lines with different endpoints. The data center tie is clear, so DataCenter would be yes once a pipeline is formally proposed. Watch for a pipeline right-of-way application, a gas supply deal, or an engineering award. Not found: any permit filing or contract for the pipeline itself.
